title: Is the lace enough for the border?
description: Two fifths of a metre and three fourths of a metre of lace are added with a common bottom number of twenty. The total is then compared with the one metre border.
teaching_notes: One idea: add the two lengths after making the fractional units the same, then compare the total with one whole. Watch for students who forget to compare with the border.

video_script.why: A learner uses the solved method on a real problem: add two fractions with a common bottom number, then compare the total with one whole.
video_script.anchor: a table cloth with a border one metre long, and two pieces of lace of different lengths

final_answer.value: Total lace = 23/20 m = 1 3/20 m. Yes, it is sufficient (it is more than 1 m).
final_answer.spoken: the total is twenty-three twentieths of a metre, which is one and three twentieths metres, and yes, the lace is enough

video_script.fraction_reading: two fifths, three fourths, eight twentieths, fifteen twentieths, twenty-three twentieths, three twentieths

names.{{NAME_8}}: person in the book problem who buys two fifths of a metre of lace

never_show: the total length before the step that adds the top numbers
maths_rules: 5 and 4 share no factor, so the common bottom number is 20
1 metre = 20/20 and 23/20 > 20/20, so the lace is enough, with 3/20 metre to spare
video_script.design: A table cloth with a one metre border stays on the board with two pieces of lace. Each length is rewritten in twentieths, the top numbers are added, and the total is compared with twenty twentieths.

narration: <bookmark mark='add'/>Step one, the total lace is two fifths plus three fourths of a metre.

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step two, two fifths is eight twentieths, using four.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Three fourths is fifteen twentieths, using five.
<bookmark mark='add'/>Step three, add the top numbers. Eight plus fifteen is twenty-three, so the total is twenty-three twentieths of a metre.

narration: <bookmark mark='split'/>Step four, twenty twentieths make one whole, so twenty-three twentieths is one and three twentieths metres.

narration: <bookmark mark='border'/>Step five, compare with the border. One metre is twenty twentieths, and twenty-three twentieths is greater.
